edition: Health news digest – Tuesday, 24 November 2026 – Morning edition

items.title: Allergy & Asthma Network Highlights Patient-Centered Research Addressing Critical Gaps in Asthma Care at ACAAI 2026
items.summary: Allergy & Asthma Network led or contributed to four abstracts at the ACAAI 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting (12-16 November, Phoenix). The studies address asthma education beyond medication, barriers to biologic adoption in severe asthma, risks of long-term steroid use, and under-recognition of uncontrolled asthma.

items.title: Repeated Exposure to Near-Ambient PM2.5 Decreases Pulmonary Function: Controlled Human Exposure Study
items.summary: A double-blind controlled study exposed healthy volunteers to PM2.5 at 35 µg/m³ on three consecutive days. Lung function fell after days 2 and 3, and effects persisted at least 20 hours after exposure ended. Published online 19 October, in issue 3 November 2026.

items.title: Who Gets Screened for Lung Cancer? Northwestern Medicine Researchers Say it's Time to Rethink the Answer
items.summary: Northwestern Medicine reported early findings from its universal age-based lung cancer screening approach. 40% of patients had a smoking history but were ineligible under USPSTF criteria, 54% had nodules or other findings warranting surveillance, and six early-stage cancers were diagnosed, including two stage 1 cancers in people who never smoked.

items.title: FDA Approves Nelkarmi for ALK-Positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
items.summary: The FDA approved neladalkib (Nelkarmi), a kinase inhibitor, for adults with previously treated locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC. The approval was based on the phase 1/2 ALKOVE-1 trial, whose primary efficacy analysis included 222 patients.
